PHI-safe, LLM-oriented code book for a data frame

Source: R/codebook.R
llm_codebook.Rd

Summarises the structure of a data frame - variable names, classes, roles, missingness, cardinality, factor levels and the shape of numeric variables - in a compact, machine-parseable form intended to be pasted into a large language model prompt. No row-level data is emitted, and columns whose names suggest direct identifiers have their values withheld.

Usage

llm_codebook(
  data,
  name = deparse(substitute(data)),
  format = c("markdown", "yaml", "json"),
  detail = c("safe", "structure", "full"),
  max_levels = 12L,
  phi_extra = NULL,
  no_redact = character(0),
  labels = NULL,
  file = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, tibble or data.table.

name

Dataset name to print. Defaults to the deparsed data argument.

format

Output format: "markdown" (default), "yaml" or "json".

detail

Level of value detail: "safe" (default), "structure" or "full". See Disclosure control.

max_levels

Maximum number of distinct values listed for a discrete variable. Above this, only the count is reported.

phi_extra

Character vector of extra regular-expression alternatives treated as identifier-like column names.

no_redact

Character vector of column names exempt from the identifier-name heuristic.

labels

Optional named character vector of variable descriptions, added to each variable's notes.

file

Optional path. When supplied, the code book is written there and returned invisibly.

Value

A length-one character vector of class llm_codebook. Returned invisibly when file is supplied.

Details

Each variable is tagged with a role, which tells a code-writing model how the column is most likely to be used:

id

unique and complete discrete column; a candidate row key

binary

logical, or exactly two distinct observed values

categorical

factor with more than two levels

numeric

numeric / integer

date

Date or POSIXct

text

character that is not obviously categorical

constant

a single observed value

empty

no observed values

Disclosure control

detail = "safe" (the default) reports numeric variables as a range and median rounded to three significant digits and dates to month precision, and lists distinct values only for low-cardinality discrete variables. detail = "structure" omits values entirely. detail = "full" reports exact numeric summaries and exact date ranges and should only be used when minimum and maximum values are not themselves disclosive. Name-based identifier redaction is applied at every detail level. The heuristic is a convenience, not a guarantee: review the output before sharing it.

Integer64 columns

bit64::integer64 columns, commonly imported from Parquet, are converted to double precision only for numeric summaries. The input data and reported column classes are unchanged. Integers outside the exactly representable range of doubles (approximately +/-2^53) may lose precision, even with detail = "full"; the conversion emits a warning in that case.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  patient_mrn = sprintf("M%05d", 1:20),
  age = c(rep(c(55, 61, 70, 48), 5)),
  sex = factor(rep(c("F", "M"), 10)),
  visit_date = as.Date("2020-01-01") + 1:20
)
llm_codebook(df)
#> # Codebook: df
#> 
#> - rows: 20
#> - columns: 4
#> - class: data.frame
#> - complete rows: 20 (100.0%)
#> - detail level: safe (row-level data withheld)
#> 
#> ## Variables
#> 
#> | variable | class | role | n_missing | %missing | n_distinct | values / summary | notes |
#> |---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
#> | `patient_mrn` | character | id | 0 | 0 | 20 | <unique identifier: values withheld> | flagged as possible direct identifier |
#> | `age` | numeric | numeric | 0 | 0 | 4 | ~range=[48, 70] ~median=58 | only 4 distinct values; may be categorical |
#> | `sex` | factor | binary | 0 | 0 | 2 | ["F", "M"] |  |
#> | `visit_date` | Date | date | 0 | 0 | 20 | range=[2020-01, 2020-01] | unique in every row |
#> 
#> ## Dataset notes
#> 
#> - candidate row identifier(s): patient_mrn
#> - values shown are aggregate metadata only; no row-level data is included
#> - columns whose names suggest direct identifiers have their values redacted
llm_codebook(df, format = "yaml", detail = "structure")
#> dataset: "df"
#> rows: 20
#> columns: 4
#> class: "data.frame"
#> complete_rows: 20
#> detail: "structure"
#> variables:
#>   - name: "patient_mrn"
#>     class: "character"
#>     role: "id"
#>     n_missing: 0
#>     pct_missing: 0
#>     n_distinct: 20
#>     values: null
#>     notes:
#>       - "flagged as possible direct identifier"
#>   - name: "age"
#>     class: "numeric"
#>     role: "numeric"
#>     n_missing: 0
#>     pct_missing: 0
#>     n_distinct: 4
#>     values: null
#>     notes:
#>       - "only 4 distinct values; may be categorical"
#>   - name: "sex"
#>     class: "factor"
#>     role: "binary"
#>     n_missing: 0
#>     pct_missing: 0
#>     n_distinct: 2
#>     values: null
#>   - name: "visit_date"
#>     class: "Date"
#>     role: "date"
#>     n_missing: 0
#>     pct_missing: 0
#>     n_distinct: 20
#>     values: null
#>     notes:
#>       - "unique in every row"
#> dataset_notes:
#>   - "candidate row identifier(s): patient_mrn"
#>   - "values shown are aggregate metadata only; no row-level data is included"
#>   - "columns whose names suggest direct identifiers have their values redacted"
